name: XMonitor - Sentiment Cheat Sheet Review Staging
description: Weekly staging job that turns hand-labelled replies into a draft per-client sentiment cheat sheet and sends it to Telegram for human activation. Drafts never affect labelling until activated.

parameters.query:
-- One row per active client that has enough hand-labelled replies to learn from.
-- Returning 0 rows is the correct "nothing to review this week" signal: every
-- downstream node simply does not run. No alwaysOutputData here on purpose.
WITH active_sheet AS (
  -- MUST filter on status. Selecting the highest version regardless of status
  -- would build each week's draft on top of last week's unapproved draft,
  -- compounding changes a human deliberately rejected. Only what is actually
  -- live is a valid starting point.
  SELECT client_id, version, rules_text
  FROM public."Sentiment Cheat Sheets"
  WHERE status = 'active'
),
-- Most recent 200 labels PER CLIENT, so a busy client cannot starve a quiet one.
recent AS (
  SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT r.client_id, r.text, r.sentiment, r.manual_sentiment,
           r.manual_sentiment_note, r.manual_labeled_at,
           row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY r.client_id
                              ORDER BY r.manual_labeled_at DESC) AS rn
    FROM public."Replies" r
    WHERE r.manual_sentiment IS NOT NULL
  ) ranked WHERE rn <= 200
),
labels AS (
  SELECT
    client_id,
    count(*)::int AS label_count,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE sentiment IS DISTINCT FROM manual_sentiment)::int
      AS disagreement_count,
    min(manual_labeled_at) AS labels_from,
    max(manual_labeled_at) AS labels_to,
    jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
      'text',  left(coalesce(text, ''), 400),
      'model', sentiment,
      'human', manual_sentiment,
      'note',  left(coalesce(manual_sentiment_note, ''), 300)
    ) ORDER BY manual_labeled_at DESC) AS examples
  FROM recent
  GROUP BY client_id
),
recipients AS (
  SELECT client_id, array_agg(DISTINCT telegram_chat_id) AS chat_ids
  FROM public."Tracked Users"
  WHERE is_active AND telegram_chat_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY client_id
)
SELECT
  c.id::text                     AS client_id,
  c.name                         AS client_name,
  COALESCE(a.version, 0)         AS current_version,
  COALESCE(a.rules_text, '')     AS current_rules,
  l.label_count,
  l.disagreement_count,
  l.labels_from,
  l.labels_to,
  l.examples,
  COALESCE(rc.chat_ids, ARRAY[]::text[]) AS chat_ids
FROM public."Clients" c
JOIN labels l ON l.client_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN active_sheet a ON a.client_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN recipients rc ON rc.client_id = c.id
WHERE c.is_active
  -- Below this, a "pattern" is noise. Skipped clients simply wait a week.
  AND l.label_count >= 15;

values.content:
You write labelling cheat sheets for a Lebanese Arabic sentiment classifier.

You receive the current cheat sheet plus replies a human reviewer relabelled,
split into ones the model got WRONG and ones it got right.

Produce an updated cheat sheet that would have fixed the wrong ones without
breaking the right ones.

Hard rules:
- Only write a rule you can trace to at least two of the wrong examples. One
  example is an anecdote, not a pattern. Never invent rules.
- Prefer flat, mechanical rules: "praise for X => Negative". Avoid nuance the
  model has to reason about.
- Keep the whole sheet under 200 words. It is sent on every analyzer call, for
  every post. Drop the weakest rule rather than growing.
- Keep rules from the current sheet that the examples still support. Silently
  dropping a working rule is a regression.
- Write rules in English even though the replies are not.

Return valid JSON only, in exactly this shape:
{"rules_text": "...", "changes": "one line on what you changed and why"}

parameters.query:
-- Stored as a DRAFT. It has no effect on labelling until a human activates it:
-- Get Active Cheat Sheets in the scheduler filters on status = 'active'.
-- The version is computed inside the INSERT so two runs cannot collide on
-- sentiment_cheat_sheets_client_version_key.
INSERT INTO public."Sentiment Cheat Sheets"
  (client_id, version, status, rules_text, source_label_count,
   generated_from, generated_to)
SELECT
  $1::uuid,
  COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) + 1,
  'draft',
  $2,
  $3::int,
  $4::timestamptz,
  $5::timestamptz
FROM public."Sentiment Cheat Sheets"
WHERE client_id = $1::uuid
RETURNING id::text AS draft_id, version;
